newsitem.title: CANADA: Teklogix ups profile with strong numbers.
newsitem.headline: Teklogix ups profile with strong numbers.

text.p: Teklogix International Inc stock has enjoyed a sharp run-up in recent weeks, which analysts and a company executive attributed as much to its strong financials as to its higher profile in the investment community.
After meandering around the 12 to 13 mark for a good part of 1996, the wireless communications company began climbing in mid-August to reach a high of 16.90 in late September.
Teklogix was unchanged at 16 on the Toronto Stock Exchange in afternoon trading on Wednesday. Analysts' projected one-year target price for the stock ranged from 18 to 22.25, company documents said.
Yorkton Securities analyst Byron Berry said investors and major important market analysts were starting to take notice of the company and its string of strong quarterly results.
"It was trading at a depressed level before this," said Berry. "It was perhaps undercovered."

Gordon Wilde, Teklogix's chief financial officer, attributed the stock gain to a recent US$6.8 million contract with the Chicago police force, a positive report by the influential investment house CIBC Wood Gundy and the hiring of a Toronto public relations firm, Media Profile.

Wilde said the company, with the aid of the new public relations firm, has been the subject of number of stories in the Canadian media, which has helped its profile. Renewed attention by analysts also appeared to be reawakening the investment community to the prospects of the company that went public last September.
Teklogix has posted a more than five-fold revenue increase in four years, jumping to C$92.5 million in fiscal 1996 from C$16.6 million in 1992.

The company manufactures a variety of wireless communications equipment that allows companies to transmit data for inventory control or other uses. The Teklogix mobile computer can be used by police forces to send and retrieve information when on the road.

The company posted 31 percent revenue growth in the first quarter ended June 30. Wilde said the gain was consistent with guidance given to the investment community of 30 percent growth for revenues and earnings for fiscal 1997.
"Can this be sustained? Yes," said Wilde. "We are just scratching the surface of opportunity."
Wilde said the company was enjoying its strongest growth in Europe and predicted the company would generate C$42 million to C$45 million in Europe this year.
"Europe and particularly Western Europe have been unbelievably strong," he said.

Analyst Berry is projecting earnings per share of about C$0.76 for fiscal 1997 and has raised his 1998 estimate from his previous C$1.04 a share level because of stronger prospects. He declined, however, to release his new estimate for 1998.
In 1996, the company earned C$8.1 million or C$0.66 a share on revenues of C$92.5 million.
